newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-VOELKER HEADS FOR MORE GOLD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-VOELKER HEADS FOR MORE GOLD.

text.p: Sandra Voelker, who won two gold medals on Friday, set herself up for two more with pace-setting heat times at the European sprints and short-course swimming championships on Saturday.

Voelker, who broke the European women's 100 metres freestyle short-course record and anchored the German 4x50 freestyle relay to victory on Friday, led qualifiers for the afternoon's finals in the Neptun pool in the 100 metres butterfly and 50 freestyle.

Voelker, 100 freestyle silver medallist and 50 freestyle bronze medallist at the Atlanta Olympics, clocked one minute 0.09 seconds in the 100 butterfly, appreciably faster than the next-best 1:00.88 of Sweden's Johanna Sjoberg.
Sjoberg beat Voelker for Friday's 50 butterfly gold when both swam under the previous European short-course record time but the 22-year-old German should have the edge in the 100.
Voelker was soon back in the water again for the 50 freestyle, clocking 25.12 to lead the way to the final ahead of Norway's Vibeke Johansen (25.29) and Britain's Susan Rolph (25.37).
But there was no place in the final for Olympic finalists Linda Olofsson of Sweden and Nina Meshcheryakova of Russia, who both failed to make the top six.
Rolph, silver medallist behind Voelker in the 100 freestyle, looked ready to challenge the 100 individual medley short-course world record in the afternoon's finals.

She clocked 1:01.40 in the heats, threatening the 1:01.03 world mark of Sweden's Louise Karlsson, who pulled out of these championships at the last minute because of a heavy cold. Nobody else came within a second of Rolph's heat time.
But fellow Briton Mark Foster cut it fine in the men's 50 butterfly, snatching the sixth and last place in the final with a time of 24.70 -- more than a second outside his world short-course best.
